scope: Machine-readable acceptance matrix for the 0.9 closeout. It fixes (a) the formal 0.9.0 release-manifest requirements that the historical v0.9.0-beta tag does not satisfy, (b) the remaining 0.9.x evidence gates, (c) the minimal serial DSH 0.1.5-rc.1 closeout slices with per-blocker owner/reproduction/acceptance/failure-closure, and (d) the ADR-0082/0083 sufficiency items. All statuses are read at the base commit. Proposed ADRs stay Proposed and nothing here is implemented.

dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.title: Independent out-of-process continuable child crash
dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.implementation_owner: D15 remediation / candidate-qualification slice D15-4 (evidence-only native harness, or the isolated runtime-adapter stack with a real DSH child process). NOT owned by post-GO R6. If 0.1.5-rc.1 has no independent-process continuable provider, this is an EXTERNAL BLOCKER: an upstream out-of-process provider implementing prepareContinuable must land and be qualified first, or the maintainer must choose a gate-order adjustment (see gate_order_options).

external_blocker.provider: out-of-process DSH continuable provider implementing SubagentProvider.prepareContinuable
external_blocker.consequence: Until an independent-process provider is qualified, subagent-child-crash cannot PASS and D15-G stays NO_GO. This must NOT be hidden by assigning the blocker to a post-gate R-series phase.

reproduction.steps: The composed native spawn provider runs children in-process; a child-only SIGKILL while the parent executor stays alive is not reachable. The owning-process SIGKILL is not a substitute.

acceptance_criteria: A real independently killable child process exists and is SIGKILLed while the parent executor stays alive.
The parent observes a truthful failed settlement for that child, retains the durable child id and can natively resume or explicitly mark loss.
Measured exactly-once settlement and no orphan process/session after cleanup.
failure_closure_criteria: If no out-of-process continuable provider can be qualified, the blocker stays BLOCKED; it may not be deleted or downgraded to optional.
Any PASS requires a real child PID death and a real parent observation, not a simulated or reasoned result.
depends_on: d15-4-child-provider-remediation (external blocker if no out-of-process provider exists)

dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.title: BYQ adapter restart rebinds a persisted continuable child
dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.implementation_owner: D15 remediation / candidate-qualification slice D15-4 candidate composition hookup under ADR-0082: the candidate profile plus a BYQ child-resume/rebind surface. NOT owned by post-GO R6. Requires an accepted ADR-0082 option (candidate-specific, reversible).

reproduction.steps: Generation A returns a continuable child and persists it. A fresh adapter exposes only root resume_session; the byte-identical 0.1.2 Python SDK has no child operation; no committed BYQ surface rebinds the child.

acceptance_criteria: After an adapter restart a fresh adapter rebinds the exact persisted continuable child and delivers messages to it.
Exactly-once settlement, original-goal linkage, BYQ-owned child-id persistence, epoch/generation fencing and orphan cleanup are all measured.
The child is never re-created as a new unrelated child and no second session store is introduced.
failure_closure_criteria: Without an accepted ADR-0082 option the blocker stays BLOCKED.
A stale-epoch or wrong-owner rebind must fail closed and be recorded, never fabricated.
depends_on: d15-4-child-provider-remediation (when option 1 is required) OR d15-4-candidate-composition-hookup

dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.title: BYQ TerminalAttachment survives an adapter restart
dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.implementation_owner: D15 remediation / candidate-qualification slice D15-5 candidate attachment layer under ADR-0083 (candidate-specific, reversible, evidence-only). R4 later productizes the attachment surface; the blocker is NOT owned by post-GO R4.

reproduction.steps: An adapter abort kills the DSH runtime. Native terminal sessions are process-local and the committed BYQ tree persists no TerminalAttachment, so a fresh adapter rejects the old attachment (real rejection evidence, no fabricated reattach).

acceptance_criteria: A BYQ-owned durable TerminalAttachment record (BYQ-minted id, owner principal, generation, executor epoch) is persisted and authorized by BYQ, not by DSH.
After an adapter restart the same attachment is rebound when native state survives, otherwise the status is truthfully lost/interrupted, never reattached.
Foreign-session and unauthorized-principal access are rejected; stale generation/epoch is fenced; cleanup leaves no orphan PTY.
Browser reaches the surface only through Gateway/Product API; no raw PTY handle or DSH event is projected.
failure_closure_criteria: Without an accepted ADR-0083 the blocker stays BLOCKED.
Any 'reattached' result must bind a real attachment/session/pid; otherwise it must be lost/interrupted.

dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.title: Truthful terminal loss across a DSH runtime restart
dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.implementation_owner: D15 remediation / candidate-qualification slice D15-5 candidate attachment layer under ADR-0083 (candidate-specific, reversible, evidence-only). R4 later productizes the attachment surface; the blocker is NOT owned by post-GO R4.

reproduction.steps: A restarted DSH runtime is a new process and native terminal sessions do not survive it; no BYQ reconnect surface exists, so the old attachment must be reported lost.

acceptance_criteria: The BYQ attachment layer records the transition to lost/interrupted and never claims reattach when the native runtime state is gone.
Orphan detection reconciles a surviving PTY with no attachment as lost, never silently reused.
Lifetime of the terminal never defines conversation or durable-job lifetime.
failure_closure_criteria: Without an accepted ADR-0083 the blocker stays BLOCKED.
A fabricated reattach fails the fail-able observer and the verdict must be non-zero.

dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.title: D15-G re-run after all four atomic blockers resolve
acceptance_criteria: All required atomic capabilities derive PASS from committed evidence; aggregates derive from their atomic members; optional host-reboot stays a limitation.
The verdict is GO only when no required atomic capability is non-PASS.
GO does not switch the production selector; the production default decision is separate.
failure_closure_criteria: Any required atomic non-PASS forces NO_GO and must name an actionable blocker.
Partial-PASS aggregation into GO must be rejected by the observer.

dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.title: R3 Thin Runtime Supervisor
acceptance_criteria: Only RuntimeGeneration health, executor epoch/fencing, native attach/resume, native-resume fallback, lifecycle observation and resource cleanup.
Not a conversation store, DSH session-store substitute, subagent persistence or PTY runtime.
dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.stop_condition: Stop at Draft PR; no production selector switch.

dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.title: R4 TerminalAttachment productization
acceptance_criteria: Attachment lifecycle, not a terminal runtime; BYQ owns identity/state/auth/reconnect.
dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.stop_condition: Stop at Draft PR; no production selector switch.

dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.title: R5 DurableJob independence
acceptance_criteria: DurableJob does not depend on Browser/Frontend/AgentSession/RuntimeGeneration/DSH process/TerminalAttachment.

dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.title: R6 Full Runtime Continuity Qualification
acceptance_criteria: Full continuity qualification over the reordered roadmap; completion does not imply a production cutover.

dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.title: Independent Production Go/No-Go
acceptance_criteria: Explicit maintainer decision on switching the production default to a qualified DSH release.
'Compatible with 0.1.5-rc.1' and 'production default = 0.1.5-rc.1' remain independent decisions.
dsh_0_1_5_rc1_closeout_slices.stop_condition: Requires explicit maintainer decision; never automatic.

findings: ADR-0082 is a decision gate that lists two options but does not by itself resolve either subagent blocker.
child-crash cannot be resolved by option 2 (in-process children); it requires option 1, an upstream out-of-process continuable provider that 0.1.5-rc.1 does not ship.

Option 2 requires a BYQ child-resume bridge; the ADR names exactly-once settlement, original-goal linkage, orphan cleanup and an epoch fence but does not define tenant/owner scoping, the authorization model, the idempotency/at-most-once contract, the fencing-token format, crash reconciliation, rollback or a testable acceptance matrix.
The ADR does not state whether acceptance authorizes a candidate-specific evidence-only implementation sufficient to re-run D15-G, which the D15-G gate requires before R3.
required_revisions: Declare which option is chosen and its feasibility owner/timeline; if option 1 is required for child-crash, state that the blocker cannot be resolved until an out-of-process continuable provider is qualified.
For option 2, add tenant/workspace scoping, authorization matrix, at-most-once settlement contract, epoch/generation fencing token, crash/orphan reconciliation, rollback and acceptance criteria.
State explicitly that acceptance authorizes only a candidate-specific, reversible qualification path to re-run D15-G, not a production default switch.

Resolve the circular ownership: the D15-G blockers must be owned by pre-gate D15 candidate-qualification slices, not by post-GO R6. If child-crash remains an external blocker, record it as such and add a maintainer gate-order option (keep / split / reorder / reclassify) instead of claiming a strictly serial executable order.
ADR-0082.gate_order_dependency: d15-4-child-provider-remediation -> d15-4-candidate-composition-hookup -> d15-g-rerun; no post-gate R-series owner.

findings: ADR-0083 correctly fixes BYQ-owned attachment identity/state/auth/reconnect and DSH-owned PTY/shell/I/O, and requires lost/interrupted instead of fabricated reattach.
It defers durable-attachment persistence to 'a separate named decision' while the blockers (adapter restart, DSH runtime restart) require exactly that persistence to be qualified.

It does not define the tenant/workspace authorization matrix, at-most-once unique attachment creation/attach, the fencing-token format, orphan GC, rollback, or the migration path for the new attachment state.
It does not resolve the sequence tension: the terminal blockers gate D15-G before R3, while productization belongs to R4 after R3.
required_revisions: Name the persistence store decision (or explicitly authorize a candidate-specific evidence-only store for D15-G) without introducing a second session store.
Add tenant/workspace authorization matrix, idempotent unique attach, epoch/generation fencing token semantics, orphan GC and rollback.
Define the candidate-specific evidence path that lets D15-G pass terminal-adapter-restart / dsh-runtime-restart before R4 productionization.
State that the terminal attachment layer needed by D15-G is a pre-gate D15-5 candidate-qualification slice, with R4 only productizing it after D15-G GO; do not assign the blocker to post-gate R4.

serial_order: 0.9 closeout audit (this batch: fact audit + plan/STATUS revision + matrix + audit tests)

d15-4-child-provider-remediation (B1; external blocker if no out-of-process provider)
concurrency: strictly serial for slices 1-5; slices 1-2 share ADR-0082 and slices 3-4 share ADR-0083, but within each pair the child/attachment boundary and its persistence must be made coherent before D15-G can be re-run.
stop_conditions: Every slice: one isolated worktree/branch/Draft PR; stop at Draft; no push to main; human merge gate.
No production selector switch, no deployment, no tag/release, no accepted-ADR change without an explicit maintainer decision.
No blocker may be deleted or downgraded to optional to obtain a GO.
No historical evidence, immutable manifest or old tag may be modified.
